coaching.title: Today's Run
coaching.message: You're 40 days out and in taper—this is the wrong week to be doing 14 miles at 122 bpm avg. Yesterday's long run was solid for peak phase, but you're still carrying volume when you should be cutting 30–40% and prioritizing recovery. Today (Sunday) do 6–8 miles easy, Z2 only (140 bpm ceiling), with 800–1200 ft vert over rolling terrain—enough to keep your legs sharp and test your fueling without compounding fatigue. Your resting HR dropped to 59 (vs. 30-day avg 65.2), which is excellent and signals adaptation, but don't squander it by repeating Peak-phase volume in Taper.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: Your sleep efficiency is high (92.2%) but duration is down slightly (7.6h vs. 8.36h avg). Taper weeks demand aggressive fueling to support glycogen supercompensation and nervous-system recovery. Eat 5–7g carbs per kg bodyweight today (assume ~70kg, so 350–490g carbs split across 4–5 meals); prioritize rice, oats, and fruit. During the 6–8 mile run, take 150–180 kcal (30–40g carbs) at mile 3 to practice your race-day aid-station routine on the easier terrain Julian Alps will demand.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: You have no HRV data on file, so focus on sleep volume and quality instead. Aim for 8.5–9 hours tonight—taper weeks are when sleep becomes performance. Legs will feel heavy and flat; that's normal and desirable. Ice-bath or contrast shower (10 min) if travel logistics allow, otherwise 15 min of easy static stretching (hamstrings, hip flexors, calves) and foam roll for 2 min per leg. No strength work today. Sunday evening: elevate legs for 20 min while digesting dinner.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: Taper paranoia hits hard at 40 days out. You're slower, tired, and second-guessing your fitness—all signs the plan is working. The dropped resting HR and 85/100 recovery score confirm your aerobic engine is primed. Respect the taper. No long efforts, no tempo, no proving anything to yourself. Your job now is to arrive in Kranjska Gora hungry and rested, not beaten down. Save the intensity for the ridgeline.
